scope: A developer/debug settings panel in client apps (iOS, macOS, Android, web, Windows/.NET): what it contains (flag overrides, A/B variant picker, analytics event log, environment info), how it is opened, and how it is kept out of release builds (compile-time exclusion vs runtime hiding), plus the security and release-engineering rules that bear on it. Out of scope: general debugger usage and crash reporting.
research_type: Technology / software (Technical MEDIUM bar: official current docs; recency matters)

questions.text: Best practices: what is current best practice for this topic?
Known solutions: what solutions, patterns, libraries and tools already exist, and how do they compare?
Platform guidelines: what do the platform owners' own guidelines say, for each platform the topic touches (Apple, Android, Windows, web, the databases and runtimes concerned)?
The expert's view: if we hired an expert consultant in this topic, what would they tell us: what to do, what to avoid, and what people usually get wrong?

methodology.method: guidelines/researching/process/research-methodology-and-sources: orient, go to authoritative sources (platform-owner docs and policies from Apple, Google/Android, Microsoft, Node.js, the build-tool projects; OWASP and MITRE for security), corroborate across independent sources, record provenance at generation time.
methodology.search_strategy: WebSearch for each platform owner's documentation and security catalogue entry; each cited page fetched with WebFetch or curl (Apple docs via their JSON endpoints; Microsoft, Vite, webpack, React Native, Swift docs as raw Markdown from their official repositories; tool READMEs raw from GitHub) and quotes copied from the fetched text.
methodology.inclusion: Primary: platform-owner documentation and store policy, language references, build-tool documentation, OWASP MAS and MITRE CWE, vendor docs for their own tools, tool READMEs for what those tools do. Secondary only where no primary covers the point (martinfowler.com feature-toggles article; Dave DeLong's post for the Xcode DEBUG default), flagged in each trust basis.
methodology.exclusion: Search-result snippets; pages that could not be fetched (OWASP MASWE-0067 returned 404; OWASP Top 10 A05 page is JavaScript-rendered and returned no text); blogs and SEO articles; any claim without a fetched quote.
methodology.scoring: guidelines/researching/evidence/verification-and-trust-scoring: Authority 30 + Independent corroboration 25 + Accuracy 20 + Currency 10 + Transparency 15, capped by the Technical (MEDIUM) domain bar; secondary sources scored at most 72.

summary: The topic's core holds: debug and test features must not be reachable in release builds (Google's Android security guidance, CWE-489, Apple App Review 2.5.19), and compile-time guards (Swift #if with Xcode's DEBUG condition, C# #if DEBUG and [Conditional], Vite import.meta.env.DEV, webpack's DefinePlugin NODE_ENV) remove the code from release. Flag-override, variant-override, event-log and environment-info functions are what existing tools provide (GrowthBook DevTools, Firebase DebugView, Pulse, FLEX). The TypeScript rule's Ctrl+Shift+D shortcut is contradicted: Chrome binds it. The topic is missing: compile code out rather than hide it at runtime (Android: not-exported is no protection); give the panel to internal/staging and TestFlight builds, not only Debug; release builds non-debuggable with debug logging off and redacted; flag-SDK dev modes and developer exception pages off in production; no secrets in client-side debug config; filter debug traffic out of analytics; guard production-time overrides; pick access gestures that do not collide with system gestures (shake is iPhone undo); on Android, BuildConfig is not generated by default since AGP 8, so prefer debug source sets or enable it; on Node servers NODE_ENV is always production.
open_questions: Whether the panel should be Debug-only or also present in internal/staging/TestFlight builds: Google recommends a dedicated staging build and Pulse targets test builds, while `#if DEBUG` alone removes it from TestFlight (Release-configuration) builds; the owner decides which configuration the rule names.

No source mandates that every app MUST include a debug panel; the requirement is a cookbook policy choice, supported here only in that its contents and its exclusion from release match platform and vendor practice.
Whether to keep shake as the iOS access gesture given Apple's HIG reserves shake for undo; in a Debug-only build the collision affects only developers.
limitations: No Apple page fetched states that Xcode's Debug configuration presets DEBUG in SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS; that rests on a secondary source.

No first-party Apple guidance on macOS debug menus was found; the macOS 'Debug menu item' access method is supported only by FLEX's mention of a debug menu item and by the general #if DEBUG mechanism.
OWASP MASWE-0067 (debuggable app) could not be fetched (404); OWASP Top 10 A05 page could not be read (JavaScript-rendered).
OWASP MASTG-TEST-0084 and MASTG-TEST-0039 are deprecated v1 tests; quoted for their stated principle only.
The maintenance status of Hyperion-Android and FLEX was not established.
No Windows (WinUI/WPF) platform-owner guidance specific to debug settings pages was found beyond the C# language reference.
license: MIT (this research record); quoted material remains under its sources' terms and is quoted for verification.

claims.question: best-practices

claims.quote: Releasing production builds that include Testing or Debug features can negatively impact the security posture of the application. These functionalities are used to help developers discover and identify bugs within intended application use cases prior to, or after a new version release, and shouldn't be publicly accessible.

claims.question: best-practices

claims.quote: Test or debug functionalities should never be implemented within production application components such as activities, broadcast receivers, services or content providers since, if exported, can be run by any other process on the device. Setting the debug component as not exported ( android:exported="false" ) does not constitute a valid protection for the capabilities since any rooted device can still execute it through the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) tool if the debug option is enabled.

claims.claim: Overriding flags in production (per-request cookie, header or query parameter) lets testers check unreleased features but lets curious or malicious users flip them too; signing the override reduces but does not remove the risk.
claims.quote: The downside of this per-request approach is that it introduces a risk that curious or malicious end-users may modify feature toggle state themselves. Some organizations may be uncomfortable with the idea that some unreleased features may be publicly accessible to a sufficiently determined party. Cryptographically signing your override configuration is one option to alleviate this concern, but regardless this approach will increase the complexity - and attack surface - of your feature toggling system.
claims.query: feature toggles expose current toggle configuration override

trust.basis: Secondary practitioner source (martinfowler.com), used because no primary source covers production-time overrides; consistent with GrowthBook's advice to disable dev mode in production.
